## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Statistics
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Statistics bodies
//  - Covariance, correlation, and fit bodies

library Statistics
{
    //==
    // # Statistics bodies
    //
    // Derived quantities on the univariate summary records of `statistics.types.plato`.
    // The bivariate surface — covariance, correlation and the fitted models —
    // follows in the next section.
    //
    // Scope: only relations that follow from the field definitions by identity —
    // bin geometry, the algebraic identities among the moment fields, and the
    // closed-form evaluation of a fitted model. The *estimators* (computing a
    // SummaryStatistics or a Histogram FROM a sample, quantile interpolation,
    // Spearman/Kendall correlation, the moving-average and outlier rules) are
    // deliberately absent: each depends on a sorting or accumulation surface this
    // vocabulary does not yet declare, and each has several defensible
    // conventions. See the TODO(content) notes at the end of the block.

    //==
    // # Histogram
    //
    // Convention, restated from the type: Counts[i] tallies the half-open bin
    // [Start + i*w, Start + (i+1)*w) where w is the Range extent over the bin
    // count, and the FINAL bin additionally includes the Range End.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histogram

    // The number of bins.
    BinCount(self: Histogram): Integer
        => self.Counts.Count;

    // The width of one bin: the Range extent divided by the bin count.
    // Precondition: at least one bin.
    BinWidth(self: Histogram): Number
        => self.Range.Extent / self.Counts.Count.ToNumber;

    // The total number of values tallied, across all bins. Values that fell
    // outside Range were never counted and are not represented here.
    TotalCount(self: Histogram): Integer
        => self.Counts.Reduce(0, (total, count) => total + count);

    // The lower edge of bin i: Start + i * BinWidth.
    BinStart(self: Histogram, bin: Integer): Number
        => self.Range.Start + bin.ToNumber * self.BinWidth;

    // The midpoint of bin i.
    BinCenter(self: Histogram, bin: Integer): Number
        => self.Range.Start + (bin.ToNumber + 0.5) * self.BinWidth;

    // The half-open span [BinStart(i), BinStart(i+1)) of bin i, as an interval.
    BinInterval(self: Histogram, bin: Integer): NumberInterval
        => (self.BinStart(bin), self.BinStart(bin + 1));

    // The index of the bin containing value, or -1 when value lies outside
    // Range. The Range End belongs to the final bin, per the type's convention.
    BinIndexOf(self: Histogram, value: Number): Integer
        => value < self.Range.Start || value > self.Range.End
            ? -1
            : value == self.Range.End
                ? self.Counts.Count - 1
                : ((value - self.Range.Start) / self.BinWidth).Floor.ToInteger;

    // The relative frequency of bin i: its count over the total count, in
    // [0, 1]. Precondition: the histogram tallied at least one value.
    Frequency(self: Histogram, bin: Integer): Number
        => self.Counts[bin].ToNumber / self.TotalCount.ToNumber;

    // The empirical probability density in bin i: the relative frequency
    // divided by the bin width, so that the bar areas sum to one. Precondition:
    // the histogram tallied at least one value and the bin width is positive.
    Density(self: Histogram, bin: Integer): Number
        => self.Frequency(bin) / self.BinWidth;

    //==
    // # SummaryStatistics
    //
    // Convention, restated from the type: Variance and StandardDeviation use
    // the SAMPLE (n - 1, Bessel-corrected) definition, and Kurtosis is EXCESS
    // kurtosis (a normal sample scores 0, not 3).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descriptive_statistics

    // The spread of the sample: Maximum - Minimum.
    ValueRange(self: SummaryStatistics): Number
        => self.Maximum - self.Minimum;

    // The midpoint of the extremes: (Minimum + Maximum) / 2.
    Midrange(self: SummaryStatistics): Number
        => (self.Minimum + self.Maximum) / 2.0;

    // The relative standard deviation: StandardDeviation / Mean. Meaningful
    // only for ratio-scale data with a positive mean.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_variation
    CoefficientOfVariation(self: SummaryStatistics): Number
        => self.StandardDeviation / self.Mean;

    // The standard error of the mean: StandardDeviation / sqrt(n).
    // Precondition: Count > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_error
    StandardErrorOfMean(self: SummaryStatistics): Number
        => self.StandardDeviation / self.Count.ToNumber.Sqrt;

    // The kurtosis on the raw (non-excess) scale, where a normal sample scores
    // 3. The stored Kurtosis field is the excess form.
    RawKurtosis(self: SummaryStatistics): Number
        => self.Kurtosis + 3.0;

    // The population variance implied by the stored sample variance:
    // s^2 * (n - 1) / n. Precondition: Count > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bessel%27s_correction
    PopulationVariance(self: SummaryStatistics): Number
        => self.Variance * (self.Count - 1).ToNumber / self.Count.ToNumber;

    //==
    // # RunningStatistics
    //
    // Convention, restated from the type: M2 is the running sum of squared
    // deviations from the current mean (Welford).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithms_for_calculating_variance#Welford's_online_algorithm

    // The Bessel-corrected sample variance: M2 / (n - 1). Precondition:
    // Count >= 2.
    SampleVariance(self: RunningStatistics): Number
        => self.M2 / (self.Count - 1).ToNumber;

    // The population variance: M2 / n. Precondition: Count >= 1.
    PopulationVariance(self: RunningStatistics): Number
        => self.M2 / self.Count.ToNumber;

    // The sample standard deviation: the square root of the sample variance.
    SampleStandardDeviation(self: RunningStatistics): Number
        => self.SampleVariance.Sqrt;

    //==
    // # FiveNumberSummary and BoxPlotStatistics
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five-number_summary
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_plot

    // The spread of the summary: Maximum - Minimum.
    ValueRange(self: FiveNumberSummary): Number
        => self.Maximum - self.Minimum;

    // The interquartile range: UpperQuartile - LowerQuartile.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interquartile_range
    InterquartileRange(self: FiveNumberSummary): Number
        => self.UpperQuartile - self.LowerQuartile;

    // The interquartile-range multiple defining Tukey's inner fences. 1.5 is a
    // convention, not a derived quantity: Tukey's outer ("far out") fences use
    // 3 instead, so the choice of multiplier is what these fences encode.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interquartile_range#Outliers)
    TukeyFenceMultiplier(_: Number): Number
        => 1.5;
```
